why: Both involve defending or helping with works, and the boundary between defending one's own work and helping another room's work is easy to blur in defence calls.

why.T3-031: The item is a running joke that mock-condemns a canvas image as scandalous; T3-031 covers the room's own humour carried into canvas talk, while T3-018 only decodes meaning and T3-143 only argues whether a joke offends.

why.T3-028: Sharing a PlaceBot and hoping it solves builders' problems is running scripts for the room's work (T3-028), not arguing script fairness (T3-027) or using extra accounts (T3-088).

why.T3-014: Sending builders to Discord and using r/Polska as HQ moves planning into a chat (T3-014), rather than gathering in a megathread (T3-015) or opening a new sub (T3-090).

why.T3-009: Praising everyone's work, celebrating momentum and posting the final result mark the collective work as achieved (T3-009), not merely reporting what happened (T3-073) or mourning the canvas's end (T3-117).

why.T3-137: Working on r/GreenLattice instead of the Portuguese mosaic is putting pixels into another group's build as one's own effort (T3-137), not helping while keeping the room's own work (T3-011).

why.T3-010: The item is mainly disputes over AMD, FRC, F1, Snek and other neighbours' space, with borders, go-under arrangements, and refusals (T3-010).
why.T3-195: Several concepts invoke or enforce an already-made agreement: peace negotiated at r/Polska, the agreement to go under AMD, the treaty protecting AMD, and the unanimous choice to befriend AMD.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-010 covers settling and disputing borders and space, but does not carry the material's repeated invocation and enforcement of already-made agreements (the treaty protecting AMD, reminders of the agreement, recording the unanimous choice to befriend AMD).
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-195's gate is met by concepts invoking or enforcing an existing deal: reporting peace negotiated, reminding expansionists of the agreement to go under AMD, enforcing the treaty protecting AMD, and recording the unanimous choice to befriend AMD and go under.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-195; what is lost is the element of holding neighbours to an already-made agreement, as distinct from the border itself being settled.

why.T3-020: The item works out where the AH logo should go and corrects locations (T3-020), rather than calling for hands to a chosen mark (T3-002) or sharing a template (T3-070).

why.T3-005: Austrian attacks, protecting the motherflag, coordinated defence and repelling AMD are the room defending its own work against attacks (T3-005).
why.T3-011: Requests to reinforce Snek, reports of helping defend Snek, asking for help for Slovakia, and promising to defend Snek's green squares are help sent to another room's work (T3-011).

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 covers the room's own defence against attacks, but does not carry the material's calls to send help to Snek or Slovakia and reports of helping defend a neighbour's work.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-011's gate is met by concepts where r/poland members are asked to reinforce Snek, told they helped defend Snek, asked to help Slovakia, or promise to defend Snek's green squares.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-011; what is lost is the outward help to neighbouring rooms, leaving only the defence of Poland's own flags and balls.

why.T3-081: Partition memory turned into a defence rally, Sabaton/Winged Hussars, and reclaiming the motherland cast the canvas work in national history (T3-081).
why.T3-130: Pan-Slavic flag proposal and rejection as Russian domination read national politics into the canvas (T3-130).

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-081 covers casting canvas fights as national history, but does not carry the material's debate over a Pan-Slavic flag and its rejection as Russian domination, which is national politics read into the canvas rather than a fight told as historic war.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-130's gate is met by concepts reading national politics and history into the canvas proposal: recruiting Poland to cover America with a Pan-Slavic flag, rejecting it as Russian domination, and explaining Poland's rejection through its problem with Russia.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-130; what is lost is the explicit national-political refusal of the Pan-Slavic shared flag, leaving only the rallying use of history.

why.T3-004: The item settles what the Polish picture should look like: shield or flag, naval flag objection, flag law, and design corrections (T3-004).
why.T3-113: PW anchor, coat of arms, eagle, Polish things, and Polish-Hungarian friendship are national emblems added to the flag (T3-113).

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-004 covers settling the mark's design, but does not specifically carry the material's national-emblem additions such as the PW anchor, coat of arms, eagle, Polish things, and Polish-Hungarian friendship.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-113's gate is met by concepts proposing, rejecting, or admiring national emblems and figures to be added to the Polish flag.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-113; what is lost is the national-emblem specificity, leaving only generic design settling.

why.T3-068: Changing Texas and Chile into Polish flags and replacing Indonesia's writing with 'Poland' convert neighbours' art into the room's sign (T3-068).
